summary: Milestone of 2026-10-20: trained behaviour/intent inference. Observable behaviour, recorded context and intent are separate label layers (docs/BEHAVIOR_INTENT_DATA.md). Trained channels: situation from synchronized audio and video (E28, Kinetics: late fusion macro-F1 0.730 on 294 held-out clips, visual only 0.689, audio only 0.456; the scene adds +0.073), dog vocal activity / intent from barks (E26/E27, Barkopedia: 0.222 from audio, 0.290 with the location as context; no class passes the gate), dog bark and cat meow context heads. A combination layer reports single-channel readings, the combined situation, explicit missing inputs and conflicts; no intent hypothesis reaches 'supported' on held-out data because no intent-labelled synchronized data exists (exact missing examples listed). The phone engine mirrors the intent stage (feature-level parity on 10 cases); phones remain untested. Earlier rounds: E20 home video, E21 audio, E24 cat keypoints, G1 detector (paused G1b ablation).

decisions: The phone test build uses the licence-stated TF Hub detector. Q-M2 was answered on 2026-10-19: the MediaPipe Object Detector page states no licence for the weights, so the MediaPipe detector stays research-only. On home phone video (E20) the TF Hub detector is the better one anyway.

Only vocalization types that passed the pre-set FSD50K gate (meow, bark) are shown or open/support interpretations; unvalidated confident types (purr, growl, hiss) remain in the JSON and can only block an interpretation (E21).
The on-furniture relation ships as the pre-specified containment rule; the learned head was not better (E15 follow-up).
Dog keypoints, MammalNet-trained heads, the AwA-Pose cat keypoint heads and the bark-context model stay research-only (data terms).
Server analysis is opt-in; the default path never uploads media.
